claim: GoTrue auth.getUser(jwt) fails (session_not_found / 403) once the auth.sessions row referenced by the JWT session_id claim is deleted — this is what makes Design 3's per-device revocation immediate; verify on the hosted project's GoTrue version (and confirm supabase-js surfaces it as an error the middleware turns into 401).
evidence: Verified against primary source (supabase/auth master, internal/api/auth.go): GET /user is routed `r.With(api.requireAuthentication).Route("/user", …)`; requireAuthentication → parseJWTClaims → maybeLoadUserOrSession, which does `if claims.SessionId != "" && claims.SessionId != uuid.Nil.String() { session, err = models.FindSessionByID(db, sessionId, false); if models.IsNotFoundError(err) { return apierrors.NewForbiddenError(apierrors.ErrorCodeSessionNotFound, "Session from session_id claim in JWT does not exist") } }`. So a signature-valid, unexpired JWT is rejected with HTTP 403 / code `session_not_found` on the very next /user call once the sessions row is gone. This shipped in supabase/auth v2.150.0 (2024-04-25, PR #1538 "return error if session id does not exist"); hosted users reported the 403 shortly after (auth-py issue #503, supabase-flutter #1083), and Supabase's Sessions guide documents the intended check: "You can check that the session_id claim in the JWT corresponds to a row in the auth.sessions table. If such a row does not exist, it means that the user has logged out." Logout scopes are hard deletes (models/sessions.go: LogoutSession = `DELETE FROM auth.sessions WHERE id = ?`, LogoutAllExceptMe, Logout), and refresh_tokens cascade, so refresh also fails afterwards (tokens/service.go: 400 `refresh_token_not_found` / `session_not_found` "No Valid Session Found"). Current auth release line is v2.19x, far past 2.150.0; hosted projects are auto-upgraded. supabase-js: auth-js `_getUser(jwt)` performs an HTTP `GET ${url}/user` with the jwt as bearer (no local verification) and returns `{ data: { user: null }, error }` (AuthApiError with status 403, code 'session_not_found') rather than throwing; Pantopus backend/middleware/verifyToken.js:69-74 does `const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getUser(token); if (error || !data.user) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Invalid or expired token' })` (same pattern in optionalAuth.js:64 and config/auth.js:56, supabase-js ^2.91 installed 2.103.3), so the 403 becomes a 401 to the app. Caveat on 'verify on the hosted project': the repo contains no real project ref or anon key (backend/.env absent; the only *.supabase.co ref is a test fixture that does not resolve), so I could not query /auth/v1/health for the hosted version — the version claim rests on release history + hosted-user reports, not a direct probe.
correction: Claim stands; three precision notes for the design. (1) Immediacy holds ONLY while the backend keeps calling auth.getUser(jwt) (a network round-trip to GoTrue per request). If anyone later switches verifyToken to supabase.auth.getClaims() with asymmetric keys, or to local jose/jsonwebtoken verification, the auth.sessions lookup disappears and revoked JWTs stay valid until exp (jwt_expiry=3600). Pin this in the design: 'server middleware must use getUser (or an equivalent auth.sessions existence check); getClaims/local verify only allowed if paired with a session-id allowlist check'. (2) The check is skipped when the JWT has no session_id (admin/minted tokens, `uuid.Nil`), so JWT-secret hygiene and no custom-minted user tokens are prerequisites; the check is 'row missing', not 'refresh token revoked' — timebox/inactivity expiry (Pro-plan features) is only enforced at refresh, so per-device revocation must physically delete the auth.sessions row (admin.signOut(thatDeviceJwt,'local'), admin.signOut(myJwt,'others'), or a SECURITY DEFINER SQL function / direct pg `DELETE FROM auth.sessions WHERE id = $1` keyed by the session_id stored in the trusted-device registry — the backend usually won't hold the other device's JWT). (3) Before shipping, run the two-line probe on the real project: `curl -H "apikey: $ANON" https://<ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/health` (expect version >= v2.150.0) and an e2e test: sign in, delete/logout that session, then getUser(jwt) → error.status 403, error.code 'session_not_found', and POST /refresh with its refresh token → 400 refresh_token_not_found → app 401.
